name: Sorrow Geometry — Grief Architecture Installation
creator: Yewande Osei-Przybylski
description: A permanent holographic installation occupying the decommissioned Calumet Waterworks, in which visitors move through crystalline structures that shift and fracture in response to aggregated grief data pulled anonymously from public BCI emotional registers. The forms are never the same twice — each visitor's passage subtly alters the geometry for everyone who follows. Osei-Przybylski spent eleven years collecting the emotional dataset before the installation opened in 2217.
medium: holographic installation with passive BCI emotional input
cultural_impact: Became an unofficial memorial site for the 2215 Shelf flooding disaster, drawing mourners from across all tiers and briefly collapsing social boundaries within its walls.
controversy: HelixCorp attempted to license the aggregated grief dataset for therapeutic product development; Osei-Przybylski's legal battle to block this became a landmark case in BCI emotional data ownership.
story_hooks: A character discovers their own grief signature embedded in the structure from a night they don't remember — suggesting their BCI was active during a blackout or identity disruption.
HelixCorp's data extraction team is operating covertly inside the installation, and someone needs to stop them before the lawsuit is decided.
The installation begins producing a geometry no one can account for — a pattern that appears to belong to no living person in the dataset.
